subject.title: fix(chat): fix ReDoS and XSS security vulnerabilities in canvas attribute parser

question: Should canvas shortcode security be enforced in `parseCanvasAttributes`, or should executable URL validation remain centralized in the Control UI iframe URL resolver?
rationale: The patch changes a security-sensitive parser, but current source shows the executable iframe URL boundary already exists downstream and the new parser sanitizer is incomplete.

options.title: Keep URL validation downstream
options.body: Reject the parser-level sanitizer, add tests around `resolveCanvasIframeUrl`, and keep parser changes limited to resource-exhaustion bounds if still needed.

options.title: Make parser filtering authoritative
options.body: Require generic URL/entity canonicalization, bypass tests, and real Control UI proof before accepting parser-level security filtering.

options.title: Pause for linked issue triage
options.body: Use the linked issue to decide whether any exploitable XSS remains after the existing iframe URL guard is considered.

recommendation.title: Keep URL validation downstream
recommendation.body: Reject the parser-level sanitizer, add tests around `resolveCanvasIframeUrl`, and keep parser changes limited to resource-exhaustion bounds if still needed.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the canvas/embed runtime and the existing iframe URL hardening path.
